walkthrough: Let $X$ denote the number of customers out of 10 who rate the logo as good. Since each customer rates it good with probability $p = 0.42$ independently, $X \sim \mathrm{B}(10, 0.42)$.

hints: The probability that at least one person rates the logo as good is $1 - \mathrm{P}(\text{none of the } n \text{ people rate it good})$.
The probability of zero good ratings in $n$ customers is $(1 - 0.42)^n = (0.58)^n$.
Set up the inequality $1 - (0.58)^n > 0.995$ and rearrange to $(0.58)^n < 0.005$.
Take logarithms on both sides and divide by $\ln(0.58)$, reversing the inequality sign to find the smallest integer $n$.
walkthrough: We want to find the minimum sample size $n$ such that the probability of at least one customer rating the logo as good exceeds $0.995$.

Step 1: Write down the complement event.
The complement of 'at least one person rates it good' is 'no one rates it good' in the sample of $n$ customers:
$$\mathrm{P}(X = 0) = (1 - 0.42)^n = (0.58)^n$$

Step 3: Isolate the exponential term:
$$-(0.58)^n > 0.995 - 1$$
$$-(0.58)^n > -0.005$$
Multiply by $-1$ and reverse the inequality sign:
$$(0.58)^n < 0.005$$

Step 4: Take natural logarithms on both sides:
$$\ln((0.58)^n) < \ln(0.005)$$
$$n \ln(0.58) < \ln(0.005)$$

Step 5: Solve for $n$:
Note that $\ln(0.58) \approx -0.54473$ is negative, so dividing by it reverses the inequality sign:
$$n > \frac{\ln(0.005)}{\ln(0.58)} = \frac{-5.29832}{-0.54473} \approx 9.726$$

Step 6: Determine the smallest integer $n$:
Since $n$ must be a whole number of customers, the smallest possible value is $n = 10$.
